turns.prompt_text: Can I screen share my Mac mini to my iPad mini? I have Tailscale installed on both
turns.response_html:
Yes, you can absolutely screen share your Mac mini to your iPad mini using Tailscale. Since Tailscale creates a secure peer-to-peer mesh VPN (an "overlay network"), your iPad will treat the Mac mini as if it is on the same local network, regardless of where either device is physically located.

1. Prepare your Mac mini

You need to enable the built-in screen sharing protocol on macOS so it can accept incoming connections.

  1. Open System Settings > General > Sharing.
  2. Toggle Screen Sharing to On.
  3. Click the (i) icon next to Screen Sharing.
  4. Ensure your user account is allowed access.
  5. Technical Note: macOS uses the VNC (Virtual Network Computing) protocol. If you want to use a non-Apple VNC client, click Computer Settings and enable "VNC viewers may control screen with password," then set a password.

2. Get your Mac's Tailscale IP

You will need the specific "Tailscale IP" (the one starting with 100.x.y.z) to connect.

  • Click the Tailscale icon in your Mac’s menu bar.
  • Copy the IP address listed under the device name (e.g., 100.12.34.56).

3. Choose an iPad App

Since iPadOS does not have a native "Screen Sharing" client like macOS does, you will need a third-party app. Here are the best options for your setup:

AppBest For...Key Features
Jump DesktopPerformance & ReliabilitySupports RDP, VNC, and their proprietary "Fluid" protocol. Excellent mouse/keyboard support.
ScreensMac-like ExperienceVery polished UI; feels native to the Apple ecosystem.
VNC ViewerBasic/Free UseA standard, reliable VNC client from RealVNC.

4. Connect from your iPad

  1. Open the Tailscale app on your iPad and ensure it is Connected.
  2. Open your chosen VNC/Remote Desktop app.
  3. Create a New Connection.
  4. In the "Address" or "Host" field, enter the Tailscale IP of your Mac mini.
  5. Enter your Mac's Username and Password when prompted.

5. Optimization Tips for iPad mini

  • Resolution: The iPad mini has a high pixel density. In your remote desktop app, set the resolution to "Retina" or a custom resolution that matches the iPad's aspect ratio to avoid black bars.
  • Input: If you have a Magic Keyboard or a Bluetooth mouse, Jump Desktop offers the most "desktop-like" pointer precision.
  • Stay Awake: Ensure your Mac mini is set to "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" in System Settings > Displays > Advanced, otherwise the connection will drop when the Mac sleeps.

How do you plan to use this setup most—as a secondary monitor or for full remote control while you're away?

turns.prompt_text: I’m using RVNC, but I must specify my port 5901 on my IPV6 address
turns.response_html:
When connecting via IPv6, the syntax for specifying a port changes slightly because IPv6 addresses already contain colons. To prevent the application from misinterpreting the port number as part of the address, you must wrap the IP address in square brackets.

The Correct Syntax

In the host/address field of RealVNC (RVNC), enter the address using this format:

[your:tailscale:ipv6:address]:5901

Example: If your Tailscale IPv6 address is fd7a:115c:a1e0::ab12:34cd, you would enter: [fd7a:115c:a1e0::ab12:34cd]:5901

Why Port 5901?

Standard macOS Screen Sharing typically defaults to Port 5900. If you find that you must use 5901, it usually indicates one of the following:

  • Multiple Virtual Desktops: macOS is assigning a secondary display session to that port.
  • Third-Party VNC Servers: If you are using a standalone VNC server (like Vine or TightVNC) instead of the native macOS "Screen Sharing" toggle, they often default to 5901 for the first display.
  • Port Forwarding/Tunneling: There may be a configuration in your local firewall or a manual SSH tunnel that is redirecting traffic.

Troubleshooting Tips

  1. Tailscale IPv6 Toggle: Ensure that IPv6 is enabled in your Tailscale Admin Console under "Settings" > "Global Settings." While Tailscale provides the address, the mesh network must have IPv6 support toggled on for it to route correctly.
  2. Authentication: Since you are using a third-party client (RVNC), ensure you have "VNC viewers may control screen with password" enabled in your Mac's Sharing > Screen Sharing > Computer Settings. Native Apple Screen Sharing uses different authentication that standard VNC clients sometimes struggle with.
  3. Use the Tailscale IPv4: If the bracketed IPv6 syntax continues to give you trouble, Tailscale also provides a stable internal IPv4 address (starting with 100.x.y.z). This avoids the bracket syntax entirely: 100.x.y.z:5901.
